column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|09-15|1926|Ρούντολφ Όικεν|Rudolf Eucken|Rudolf Eucken was a German philosopher. He developed a philosophy of spirit and moral action, and in 1908 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1926.

bio|09-15|1973|Γουσταύος ΣΤ' Αδόλφος|Gustaf VI Adolf|Gustaf VI Adolf was King of Sweden from 1950 to 1973. He was an archaeologist and a scholar of China, and he was the grandfather of the present king, Carl XVI Gustaf.

bio|09-15|1984|Χάρι|Prince Harry|Prince Harry was born in 1984. He is the younger son of King Charles III and Princess Diana. He served in the British Army in Afghanistan, and since 2020 he has lived in the United States with his wife, Meghan.

bio|09-15|2006|Οριάνα Φαλάτσι|Oriana Fallaci|Oriana Fallaci was an Italian journalist and writer. She became known for her interviews with leaders and for her books, such as "A Man". She died in 2006.

bio|09-16|1824|Λουδοβίκος ΙΗ΄|Louis XVIII|Louis XVIII was King of France. He was restored to the throne in 1814, after the fall of Napoleon, and reigned until 1824, with a brief interruption in 1815. He issued the "Charter" of 1814.

bio|09-16|1888|Φρανς Έμιλ Σίλανπαα|Frans Eemil Sillanpää|Frans Eemil Sillanpää was a Finnish writer. He wrote novels about rural life and in 1939 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1964.

bio|09-16|1891|Καρλ Νταίνιτς|Karl Dönitz|Karl Dönitz was a German admiral. He commanded the U-boat fleet and, after Hitler's suicide, he became head of the German state for a few days in 1945. He was convicted at the Nuremberg trial.

bio|09-16|1924|Λορίν Μπακόλ|Lauren Bacall|Lauren Bacall was born in 1924 in New York. She was an American actress and was married to Humphrey Bogart. She became known with the film "To Have and Have Not". She died in 2014.

bio|09-16|1925|Μπι Μπι Κινγκ|B. B. King|B. B. King was an American blues guitarist and singer. His guitar, which he called "Lucille", and songs such as "The Thrill Is Gone" made him famous. He died in 2015.
bio|09-16|1956|Ντέιβιντ Κόπερφιλντ|David Copperfield|David Copperfield is an American magician. He became known for his spectacular acts on television, such as making the Statue of Liberty disappear.

bio|09-16|1980|Ζαν Πιαζέ|Jean Piaget|Jean Piaget died in 1980 in Geneva. He was a Swiss psychologist who studied the development of children's thinking and described the stages of cognitive development.

bio|09-16|2025|Ρόμπερτ Ρέντφορντ|Robert Redford|Robert Redford died on 16 September 2025, at the age of 89. He was an American actor and director. He won an Oscar for directing "Ordinary People" and founded the Sundance festival.

bio|09-17|1179|Χίλντεγκαρντ του Μπίνγκεν|Hildegard of Bingen|Hildegard of Bingen was a German nun and abbess. She wrote theological and natural-science works and composed hymns. The Catholic Church honours her as a saint and as a Doctor of the Church.
bio|09-17|1665|Φίλιππος Δ΄|Philip IV|Philip IV was King of Spain from 1621 to 1665. During his reign Spain lost its supremacy in Europe. He was a patron of the painter Velázquez.

bio|09-17|1743|Κοντορσέ|Marquis de Condorcet|The Marquis de Condorcet was a French philosopher and mathematician of the Enlightenment. He wrote about the progress of the human mind and supported the rights of women. He died in 1794, in prison, during the Revolution.

bio|09-17|1826|Μπέρναρντ Ρίμαν|Bernhard Riemann|Bernhard Riemann was born in 1826 in Breselenz, Germany. He was a mathematician and developed Riemannian geometry, which Einstein later used. He died in 1866.

bio|09-17|1857|Κονσταντίν Τσιολκόφσκι|Konstantin Tsiolkovsky|Konstantin Tsiolkovsky was a Russian scientist and teacher. He is regarded as one of the founders of astronautics and formulated the rocket equation. He died in 1935.
bio|09-17|1863|Αλφρέ ντε Βινύ|Alfred de Vigny|Alfred de Vigny was a French poet and writer of Romanticism. He wrote the play "Chatterton" and the novel "Cinq-Mars". He died in 1863.

bio|09-17|1931|Αν Μπάνκροφτ|Anne Bancroft|Anne Bancroft was an American actress. She won an Oscar for "The Miracle Worker" and played Mrs Robinson in "The Graduate". She was married to Mel Brooks. She died in 2005.
bio|09-17|1968|Αναστέιζια|Anastacia|Anastacia is an American singer. She became known with hits such as "I'm Outta Love" and "Left Outside Alone".
bio|09-17|1994|Καρλ Πόπερ|Karl Popper|Karl Popper died in 1994 in London. He was an Austrian philosopher of science and argued that scientific theories must be capable of being refuted.
bio|09-18|53|Τραϊανός|Trajan|Trajan was born in Italica in Spain and was the first Roman emperor to come from a province. During his reign the empire reached its greatest extent.
bio|09-18|96|Δομιτιανός|Domitian|Domitian was a Roman emperor from 81 to 96, of the Flavian dynasty. He was assassinated on 18 September 96 in a plot at the court, and he was succeeded by Nerva.

bio|09-18|1709|Σάμουελ Τζόνσον|Samuel Johnson|Samuel Johnson was an English writer and lexicographer. He compiled the "Dictionary of the English Language" in 1755, and his biographer James Boswell wrote "The Life of Samuel Johnson". He died in 1784.

bio|09-18|1783|Λέοναρντ Όιλερ|Leonhard Euler|Leonhard Euler was a Swiss mathematician and physicist, one of the most important figures in history. He contributed to analysis, graph theory and number theory. He died in 1783.

bio|09-18|1905|Γκρέτα Γκάρμπο|Greta Garbo|Greta Garbo was a Swedish actress and one of the greatest stars of silent and sound cinema. She starred in the films "Queen Christina" and "Ninotchka". She retired in 1941. She died in 1990.
bio|09-18|1961|Τζέιμς Γκαντολφίνι|James Gandolfini|James Gandolfini was an American actor. He became known as Tony Soprano in the series "The Sopranos". He died in 2013, at the age of 51.

bio|09-18|1961|Νταγκ Χάμαρσκελντ|Dag Hammarskjöld|Dag Hammarskjöld died on 18 September 1961 when his plane crashed in Zambia, on his way to negotiations about the Congo. He was Secretary-General of the United Nations and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize posthumously.

bio|09-18|1970|Τζίμι Χέντριξ|Jimi Hendrix|Jimi Hendrix was an American guitarist and singer. He is considered one of the greatest rock guitarists, with hits such as "Purple Haze". He died in 1970, at the age of 27.

bio|09-18|1971|Λανς Άρμστρονγκ|Lance Armstrong|Lance Armstrong is a former American cyclist. He won the Tour de France seven times, but the titles were stripped in 2012, when he admitted using banned substances. He had beaten cancer and founded the Livestrong foundation.

bio|09-19|86|Αντωνίνος ο Ευσεβής|Antoninus Pius|Antoninus Pius was a Roman emperor from 138 to 161. His reign is regarded as a period of peace and stability. He was adopted by Hadrian and had Marcus Aurelius as his successor.

bio|09-19|1551|Ερρίκος Γ΄|Henry III|Henry III was King of France from 1574. He reigned during the religious wars between Catholics and Protestants. He was assassinated in 1589 by a monk, and he was the last king of the House of Valois.

bio|09-19|1710|Όλε Ρέμερ|Ole Rømer|Ole Rømer was a Danish astronomer. In 1676 he first calculated that the speed of light is finite, from the delays in the eclipses of the moons of Jupiter. He died in 1710.
bio|09-19|1881|Τζέιμς Γκάρφιλντ|James Garfield|James Garfield was the 20th president of the United States. He was shot in July 1881 and died on 19 September, after only a few months in office.
bio|09-19|1911|Ουίλιαμ Γκόλντινγκ|William Golding|William Golding was an English writer. He wrote the novel "Lord of the Flies" and in 1983 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1993.
bio|09-19|1926|Μασατόσι Κοσίμπα|Masatoshi Koshiba|Masatoshi Koshiba was a Japanese physicist. He detected neutrinos from a supernova and in 2002 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 2020.
bio|09-19|1935|Κονσταντίν Τσιολκόφσκι|Konstantin Tsiolkovsky|Konstantin Tsiolkovsky died in 1935. He was a Russian scientist and teacher and one of the founders of astronautics and of rocket theory.
bio|09-19|1948|Τζέρεμι Άιρονς|Jeremy Irons|Jeremy Irons is an English actor. He won an Oscar for "Reversal of Fortune" and played in "The Mission" and "Lolita".
bio|09-19|1985|Ίταλο Καλβίνο|Italo Calvino|Italo Calvino was an Italian writer, born in Cuba. He wrote "Invisible Cities" and "If on a winter's night a traveler". He died in 1985, of a stroke.

bio|09-20|1878|Άπτον Σίνκλερ|Upton Sinclair|Upton Sinclair was an American writer. In the novel "The Jungle" he denounced the conditions in the Chicago meat industry, and he won a Pulitzer Prize for "Dragon's Teeth". He died in 1968.
bio|09-20|1934|Σοφία Λόρεν|Sophia Loren|Sophia Loren is an Italian actress. She won an Oscar for "Two Women" by Vittorio De Sica and has played in many Italian and American films.
bio|09-20|1940|Τάρο Άσο|Taro Aso|Taro Aso is a Japanese politician. He was prime minister of Japan from 2008 to 2009 and later minister of finance.

bio|09-20|1948|Τζωρτζ Ρ.Ρ. Μάρτιν|George R. R. Martin|George R. R. Martin is an American writer and screenwriter. He wrote the novel series "A Song of Ice and Fire", which became the television series "Game of Thrones".

bio|09-20|1957|Γιαν Σιμπέλιους|Jean Sibelius|Jean Sibelius was a Finnish composer. He wrote seven symphonies and the symphonic poem "Finlandia", which became a symbol of national identity. He died in 1957.

bio|09-20|1975|Σαιν-Τζον Περς|Saint-John Perse|Saint-John Perse, whose real name was Alexis Leger, was a French diplomat and poet. In 1960 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1975.

bio|09-20|1993|Γιούλιαν Ντράξλερ|Julian Draxler|Julian Draxler is a German footballer who plays as a midfielder. He played for Schalke, Paris Saint-Germain and Flamengo, and he won the 2014 World Cup.
bio|09-20|1996|Πολ Έρντος|Paul Erdős|Paul Erdős was a Hungarian mathematician. He lived as a wanderer and wrote more than 1,500 papers with many collaborators. He died in 1996.

bio|09-21|1327|Εδουάρδος Β΄|Edward II|Edward II was King of England from 1307. He was deposed in 1327 by his wife Isabella and her lover, and he died at Berkeley Castle, according to tradition on 21 September.

bio|09-21|1558|Κάρολος Κουίντος|Charles V|Charles V was Holy Roman Emperor and King of Spain. He was one of the strongest rulers of his time and abdicated in 1556. He died in 1558 in a monastery in Spain.
bio|09-21|1832|Γουόλτερ Σκοτ|Walter Scott|Walter Scott was a Scottish writer. He is regarded as the creator of the historical novel and wrote "Ivanhoe". He died in 1832.

bio|09-21|1860|Άρθουρ Σοπενχάουερ|Arthur Schopenhauer|Arthur Schopenhauer was a German philosopher. In his work "The World as Will and Representation" he argued a pessimistic view of life. He died in 1860.

bio|09-21|1866|Χ. Τζ. Γουέλς|H. G. Wells|H. G. Wells was born in 1866 in Bromley. He was an English writer and a pioneer of science fiction, with works such as "The Time Machine" and "The War of the Worlds". He died in 1946.

bio|09-21|1909|Κβάμε Νκρούμαχ|Kwame Nkrumah|Kwame Nkrumah was the leader of Ghana in the struggle for independence and its first prime minister and president, from 1957. He supported the unity of Africa. He was overthrown in 1966 and died in 1972.
bio|09-21|1934|Λέοναρντ Κόεν|Leonard Cohen|Leonard Cohen was a Canadian poet, writer and songwriter. He wrote songs such as "Suzanne" and "Hallelujah". He died in 2016.
bio|09-21|1947|Στίβεν Κινγκ|Stephen King|Stephen King is an American writer. He writes mainly horror and fantasy novels, such as "The Shining" and "It". Many of his books have been made into films.

bio|09-21|1954|Σίνζο Άμπε|Shinzo Abe|Shinzo Abe was a Japanese politician. He was prime minister of Japan from 2006 to 2007 and from 2012 to 2020, the longest serving in the country. He was assassinated in 2022.
bio|09-22|1520|Σελίμ Α΄|Selim I|Selim I was an Ottoman sultan from 1512 to 1520. He conquered Syria and Egypt, and the sultan took the title of caliph. He was the father of Suleiman the Magnificent.

bio|09-22|1539|Γκουρού Νάνακ Ντεβ|Guru Nanak Dev|Guru Nanak was the founder of Sikhism and the first of its ten gurus. He taught the unity of God and the equality of people. He died, according to tradition, in 1539.

bio|09-22|1791|Μάικλ Φαραντέι|Michael Faraday|Michael Faraday was an English physicist and chemist. He discovered electromagnetic induction and carried out experiments on electrolysis. He died in 1867.
bio|09-22|1828|Σάκα Ζούλου|Shaka Zulu|Shaka was the leader of the Zulu in South Africa. He united the clans and created a powerful army and state. He was murdered in 1828 by his half-brothers.

bio|09-22|1842|Αμπντούλ Χαμίτ Β΄|Abdul Hamid II|Abdul Hamid II was an Ottoman sultan from 1876 to 1909. By suspending the constitution he ruled in an authoritarian way, and he was deposed after the Young Turk revolution. He died in 1918.

bio|09-22|1953|Σεγκολέν Ρουαγιάλ|Ségolène Royal|Ségolène Royal is a French Socialist politician. In 2007 she was the first woman with a major party to stand as a candidate for the French presidency, and she was defeated by Nicolas Sarkozy.

bio|09-22|1956|Φρέντερικ Σόντυ|Frederick Soddy|Frederick Soddy died in 1956. He was an English chemist who studied radioactivity and introduced the concept of isotopes. In 1921 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|09-22|1958|Αντρέα Μποτσέλι|Andrea Bocelli|Andrea Bocelli is an Italian tenor who has been blind since childhood. He became known throughout the world with the song "Con te partirò" and with many albums of classical and pop music.

bio|09-22|1976|Ρονάλντο|Ronaldo|Ronaldo Luís Nazário de Lima is a former Brazilian footballer who played as a forward. He won two World Cups, in 1994 and 2002, and the Ballon d'Or twice. He played for Barcelona, Inter and Real Madrid.

bio|09-23|-63|Οκταβιανός Αύγουστος|Augustus|Augustus was born in Rome on 23 September 63 BC and became the first Roman emperor. He was the adopted son of Julius Caesar and ruled until AD 14. His date of birth is well documented.
bio|09-23|1215|Κουμπλάι Χαν|Kublai Khan|Kublai Khan was a Mongol ruler and grandson of Genghis Khan. He founded the Yuan dynasty of China and became emperor of China. He died in 1294.

bio|09-23|1241|Σνόρρι Στούρλουσον|Snorri Sturluson|Snorri Sturluson was an Icelandic historian, poet and politician. He wrote the "Prose Edda" and the "Heimskringla", basic sources for Norse mythology. He was murdered in 1241.
bio|09-23|1371|Τσενκ Χι|Zheng He|Zheng He was a Chinese admiral and explorer. In the early 15th century he led great naval expeditions, reaching India and Africa.

bio|09-23|1491|Ζακ Καρτιέ|Jacques Cartier|Jacques Cartier was a French explorer from Brittany. He explored the Saint Lawrence in Canada. His date of birth is uncertain, because the sources give different dates. He died in 1557.

bio|09-23|1870|Προσπέρ Μεριμέ|Prosper Mérimée|Prosper Mérimée was a French writer and historian. He wrote the short story "Carmen", which inspired Bizet's opera, and he was inspector of historical monuments. He died in 1870.

bio|09-23|1930|Ρέι Τσαρλς|Ray Charles|Ray Charles was an American singer and pianist, blind from childhood. He blended jazz, blues and gospel and wrote hits such as "Georgia on My Mind". He died in 2004.

bio|09-23|1939|Σίγκμουντ Φρόυντ|Sigmund Freud|Sigmund Freud was an Austrian psychiatrist and the founder of psychoanalysis. He wrote "The Interpretation of Dreams". He left Vienna in 1938 because of the Nazis and died in London in 1939.

bio|09-23|1973|Πάμπλο Νερούδα|Pablo Neruda|Pablo Neruda died on 23 September 1973, a few days after the coup in Chile. He was a poet and diplomat, and in 1971 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|09-24|15|Βιτέλλιος|Vitellius|Vitellius was a Roman emperor in 69, in the "Year of the Four Emperors". He held the throne for a few months and was killed by the followers of Vespasian.

bio|09-24|768|Πιπίνος ο Βραχύς|Pepin the Short|Pepin the Short was King of the Franks from 751 to 768. He was the first of the Carolingian dynasty and the father of Charlemagne. He donated lands to the Pope, the "Donation of Pepin".

bio|09-24|1541|Παράκελσος|Paracelsus|Paracelsus was a Swiss physician and alchemist. He introduced the use of chemical substances in medicine and challenged ancient theories. He died in 1541 in Salzburg.

bio|09-24|1834|Πέτρος Α΄|Peter I of Brazil|Peter I was the first emperor of Brazil, from 1822. He declared independence from Portugal and abdicated in 1831. As Peter IV he also reigned in Portugal. He died in 1834.

bio|09-24|1884|Ισμέτ Ινονού|İsmet İnönü|İsmet İnönü was a Turkish military officer and politician. He was a close associate of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, and prime minister and the second president of Turkey from 1938 to 1950. He died in 1973.
bio|09-24|1896|Φ. Σκοτ Φιτζέραλντ|F. Scott Fitzgerald|F. Scott Fitzgerald was an American writer. He wrote "The Great Gatsby" and "Tender Is the Night" and described the Jazz Age. He died in 1940.

bio|09-24|1900|Ρουχολάχ Χομεϊνί|Ruhollah Khomeini|Ruhollah Khomeini was an Iranian religious and political leader. He led the Islamic Revolution of 1979 and became Supreme Leader of Iran. The exact year of his birth is given differently in the sources. He died in 1989.

bio|09-24|1911|Κονσταντίν Τσερνιένκο|Konstantin Chernenko|Konstantin Chernenko was a Soviet politician. He was general secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1984, and he died in 1985, after less than a year.

bio|09-25|275|Αυρηλιανός|Aurelian|Aurelian was a Roman emperor from 270 to 275. He reunited the empire, which had been split apart, and raised the walls of Rome. He was assassinated in 275 by his own officers.
bio|09-25|1881|Λου Σιουν|Lu Xun|Lu Xun was a Chinese writer and a pioneer of modern Chinese literature. He wrote "Diary of a Madman" and "The True Story of Ah Q". He died in 1936.

bio|09-25|1897|Ουίλιαμ Φώκνερ|William Faulkner|William Faulkner was born in 1897 in Mississippi. He was a writer of the American South and in 1949 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1962.
bio|09-25|1906|Ντμίτρι Σοστακόβιτς|Dmitri Shostakovich|Dmitri Shostakovich was born in 1906 in Saint Petersburg. He was a composer who wrote 15 symphonies and 15 string quartets. He died in 1975.

bio|09-25|1958|Τζον Γουάτσον|John B. Watson|John B. Watson was an American psychologist and the founder of behaviourism. He argued that psychology should study only observable behaviour. He died in 1958.

bio|09-25|1968|Γουίλ Σμιθ|Will Smith|Will Smith is an American actor and rapper. He became known through the series "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air" and films such as "Men in Black", and he won an Oscar for "King Richard".

bio|09-25|1969|Κάθριν Ζέτα-Τζόουνς|Catherine Zeta-Jones|Catherine Zeta-Jones is a Welsh actress. She won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "Chicago" and played in the films "The Mask of Zorro" and "Chicago".
bio|09-25|1970|Έριχ Μαρία Ρεμάρκ|Erich Maria Remarque|Erich Maria Remarque died in 1970 in Switzerland. He was a German writer and wrote the anti-war novel "All Quiet on the Western Front".

bio|09-25|1983|Λεοπόλδος Γ΄|Leopold III|Leopold III was King of the Belgians from 1934. His stance in the Second World War, with the surrender to the Germans in 1940, caused division, and he abdicated in 1951 in favour of his son Baudouin. He died in 1983.

bio|09-26|1849|Ιβάν Παβλόφ|Ivan Pavlov|Ivan Pavlov was a Russian physiologist. He studied conditioned reflexes in experiments on dogs, and in 1904 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. He died in 1936.

bio|09-26|1888|Τόμας Στερνς Έλιοτ|T. S. Eliot|T. S. Eliot was born in St Louis and lived in England, where he became a British citizen. He was a poet, playwright and critic, and he wrote "The Waste Land". In 1948 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1965.

bio|09-26|1889|Μάρτιν Χάιντεγκερ|Martin Heidegger|Martin Heidegger was a German philosopher. He wrote "Being and Time" and influenced existentialism. He was controversial because of his membership of the Nazi party. He died in 1976.

bio|09-26|1940|Βάλτερ Μπένγιαμιν|Walter Benjamin|Walter Benjamin was a German-Jewish philosopher and critic. He took his own life on 26 September 1940, at the border between France and Spain, while fleeing the Nazis.

bio|09-26|1945|Μπέλα Μπάρτοκ|Béla Bartók|Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer and ethnomusicologist. He collected folk songs of Eastern Europe and wrote the "Concerto for Orchestra". He died in 1945 in New York.
bio|09-26|1965|Πέτρο Ποροσένκο|Petro Poroshenko|Petro Poroshenko is a Ukrainian businessman and politician. He was president of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019.

bio|09-26|1981|Σερένα Ουίλιαμς|Serena Williams|Serena Williams is an American former tennis player. She won 23 Grand Slam singles titles and for years was at the top of the world rankings. She retired in 2022.

bio|09-26|1990|Αλμπέρτο Μοράβια|Alberto Moravia|Alberto Moravia was an Italian writer. He wrote the novels "The Time of Indifference" and "Two Women", and his works were adapted for the cinema. He died in 1990.

bio|09-26|2008|Πωλ Νιούμαν|Paul Newman|Paul Newman was an American actor and director. He starred in the films "The Hustler" and "Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid" and won an Oscar in 1987. He founded a food company that gives its profits to charity. He died in 2008.

bio|09-27|1722|Σάμουελ Άνταμς|Samuel Adams|Samuel Adams was an American patriot and one of the leaders of the American Revolution. He took part in the Boston Tea Party and signed the Declaration of Independence. He died in 1803.
bio|09-27|1871|Γκράτσια Ντελέντα|Grazia Deledda|Grazia Deledda was born in 1871 in Sardinia. She was an Italian writer and in 1926 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 1936.
bio|09-27|1917|Εντγκάρ Ντεγκά|Edgar Degas|Edgar Degas died in 1917 in Paris. He was a French painter and sculptor, known for his dancers and horse races.
bio|09-27|1972|Γκουίνεθ Πάλτροου|Gwyneth Paltrow|Gwyneth Paltrow is an American actress. She won an Oscar for "Shakespeare in Love" and appeared in "Iron Man". She founded the company Goop.
bio|09-27|1976|Φραντσέσκο Τόττι|Francesco Totti|Francesco Totti is a former Italian footballer. He played his entire career for Roma and won the 2006 World Cup with Italy.
bio|09-27|1984|Αβρίλ Λαβίν|Avril Lavigne|Avril Lavigne is a Canadian singer and songwriter. She became known with hits such as "Complicated" and "Sk8er Boi", and with her pop-punk style.

bio|09-27|1996|Μοχαμάντ Νατζιμπουλάχ|Mohammad Najibullah|Mohammad Najibullah was an Afghan politician and president of Afghanistan from 1987 to 1992. When the Taliban took Kabul in 1996, they executed him.
bio|09-27|2017|Χιου Χέφνερ|Hugh Hefner|Hugh Hefner was an American publisher and the founder of the magazine Playboy, in 1953. He died in 2017.

bio|09-27|2024|Χασάν Νασράλα|Hassan Nasrallah|Hassan Nasrallah was a Lebanese cleric and secretary-general of Hezbollah from 1992. He was killed on 27 September 2024 in an Israeli air strike on Beirut.

bio|09-28|-551|Κομφούκιος|Confucius|Confucius was a Chinese philosopher. He taught ethics, filial piety and good government, and his thought deeply influenced Chinese civilisation. His date of birth, 28 September 551 BC, is based on tradition.
